newsitem.title: CHINA: HK strikes down clutch of labour rights laws.
newsitem.headline: HK strikes down clutch of labour rights laws.

text.p: Hong Kong's China-appointed parliament voted late on Wednesday to strike down a clutch of laws governing labour rights.
Members of the Provisional Legislative Council suspended four of seven laws which were enacted shortly before China took back the 156-year-old British colony on July 1.

Three of the four suspended laws govern labour rights and involve the right of unions to bargain collectively with employers on wages and benefits on behalf of employees, and to use union funds for political activity.
The remaining one deals with individual rights.

Three of the seven pre-handover laws to survive was one placing limits on harbour reclamation and two labour laws -- to increase compensation for victims of occupational deafness and to declare May 1 as a statutory holiday.
The administration of Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa had recommended the seven laws be suspended till end October to give it time to table counter-legislation.
Tung's government had argued that the laws -- five of them governing labour rights -- would harm Hong Kong's economic competitiveness.
